chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Uthman al-Misri narrated to us in Egypt, saying: Ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Al-Mufaddal ibn Fudalah narrated from Isa ibn Ibrahim, from Salama ibn Sulayman al-Khudri, from Harun ibn Salim, from Ibn Kurdoos, from his father, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'One who stays awake during the night of Eid and the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban, his heart will not die on the day the hearts die.'

key_terms.لَيْلَةَ النِّصْفِ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ: The night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban
key_terms.يَوْمَ تَمُوتُ الْقُلُوبُ: The day the hearts die (Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of staying awake on the night of the 15th of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* highlights the spiritual vitality granted by night-long worship (*qiyam*) during the Nights of Eid and specifically the *Laylat al-Nisf min Sha'ban*. In Shia tradition, this night is deeply associated with the birth of Imam al-Mahdi (aj), making the preservation of the heart from spiritual death a key eschatological promise for believers awaiting his reappearance.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2.  The Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) says, “One who stays awake during the night of Eid and of 15th  Shaban his heart would remain alive on the day the hearts are destined to die.”
